The title of the U.S. Code for the National Guard when it is not in federal service. It governs organization, federal funding, and training of the Guard while it remains under the command of state governors.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 70A Stat. 596](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/STATUTE-70A){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 32 U.S.C. 101 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/uscode/2024/title32){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Federal recognition, organization, and equipment standards for the Guard.
- Sec. 502(f): Guard members may perform training or other duty, including operational support requested by the President or Secretary of Defense, while under state command and federally paid.
- Sec. 112: counterdrug support under governors' plans.
- Chapter 9: homeland defense activities.

## Why it matters

'Title 32 status' is the middle position between purely state service and federal service under [Title 10](title10-usc.qmd): federal money and missions, state command. Because troops in that status are not federal forces, the [Posse Comitatus Act](posse-comitatus-1878.qmd) does not apply to them, which is why the choice of status under the [mobilization authorities](reserve-mobilization.qmd) is often the decisive legal question in domestic deployments. Its roots are in the [Militia Act of 1903](dick-act-1903.qmd).

## Current status

In force as positive law, enacted together with Title 10 in 1956.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}
